questions_used.question: What is the reader auditing?
questions_used.answer: Redundancy. I want to count the paths at each layer — two per MUX to the cores, both firewalls to both border leaves, both spines to each leaf, both leaves to each rack.

questions_used.question: May independent links share a bus?
questions_used.answer: Never. Each redundancy link stays its own line; if I can't count it, the diagram is wrong.

questions_used.question: One pane beside the chat, or a canvas I navigate?
questions_used.answer: One pane if the fabric reads at natural zoom; a canvas if it truly needs it. No shrinking the text.
questions_used.resolution: The annex sets the preference order and leaves the judgment to the generator. Measured: a single view of all 28 relations is 60x82 cells against a 77x47 pane (recorded/probe-single-view.stdout), so it does not read at natural zoom and the canvas rung applies. No zoom-out was used anywhere.

questions_used.question: Dots on any link?
questions_used.answer: None. The source turned them off and these are physical links.

questions_used.question: Which layers must be countable, and in which order?
questions_used.answer: four ISPs into two MUXes (two each), each MUX to both cores, both cores into both firewalls with active/standby stated, both firewalls into both border leaves, both spines into every leaf, both leaves into every rack; border leaves and rack leaves at the same level, spines above them.

questions_used.question: Must the tier levels be preserved?
questions_used.answer: Yes: border leaves and rack leaves at the same level, spines above them (source.md line 248, restated in the brief).

questions_used.question: Do the four ISP identities stay separate nodes?
questions_used.answer: Keep them separate. The framing counts four ISPs, and source.md allows folding into MUX labels only with explicit coverage; four labelled ISP nodes cost nothing in a canvas and make the 2+2 handoff countable.
questions_used.reason: The annex and framing say nothing about folding; source.md's fixed constraint permits folding only conditionally, so the safe, countable reading is four ISP nodes labelled ISP A-D.

questions_used.question: Are the arrows traffic direction or physical connectivity?
questions_used.answer: Physical connectivity; the source states it is not proof of one-way traffic, so the drawn arrow keeps the source's endpoint order and the convention is stated in generation.md.

questions_used.question: How many ISPs land on each MUX?
questions_used.answer: Two per MUX: ISP A and ISP B into MUX 1, ISP C and ISP D into MUX 2.

triage.converged_when: After the annex fixed the audit rule (count every path, never bundle), the shape preference (no shrinking), the level order (leaves level, spines above) and the motion answer (none), the only open item was whether the fabric reads at natural zoom. The recorded single-view probe measured 60x82 against 77x47, which settled it to the canvas rung; the picture was then complete and no further question could have changed a spec fact without inventing one.

routing_record.geometry_note: Two sibling boxes in one tb rank are always 3 cells apart (ACROSS_GAP_TB = 3 in rataflow/src/layout.rs), so every cell of that gap is inside ring 2 of one sibling or the other: a route that has to pass a sibling box cannot be clean there and must go around it. The shipped fabric's bl2->sp1 is a back edge whose inside hop must re-enter the spine from below (sides_for: within NEAR_RANKS = 1, tb -> (Top, Bottom)); the router paid NEAR_BAND_COST (8 per cell, rataflow/src/router.rs) for 22 cells rather than detour, which it only does when no corridor it can reach is clear.
routing_record.no_lever_removed_it: Three candidates (baseline tb, lr orientation, wider source-backed spacing) were measured; the count fell from 31 (single view) to 19, 16 and 29 cells, and always on fan-crossing routes. The budget of three spec candidates per rendered diagram is spent; the remaining defect is reported, not hidden.
